summary.name: AI Monitor
summary.one_liner: A small USB display (ESP32 board) that shows your AI service usage limits and reset times for Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Cursor and Antigravity, fed by a Mac or Windows PC.
use_cases: Watch Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor usage limits on a desk display
See when AI service quotas reset without opening an app
Track weekly and session limits at a glance while coding
Build a cheap dedicated status screen for AI usage
Show a clock when the companion app is closed
summary.what_it_does: The page describes AI Monitor, a companion app for Mac and Windows that pulls usage limits and reset times from CodexBar (or Win-CodexBar on Windows) and sends them over USB to an ESP32 display. Supported boards are the CYD 2.8-inch ESP32-2432S028 and the 480x480 Guition ESP32-S3-4848S040. On Claude, the S3 can show three quotas at once with reset times and a pace indicator comparing used share to elapsed time. The app lets you assign up to eight windows on the display, each showing an AI service or the clock, with automatic or touch-based switching. Firmware is installed from the app.
notable: Shows Claude's three quotas simultaneously on the 480x480 S3 board, with a pace indicator
Up to eight configurable display windows, switchable by tapping the screen (firmware 2.19.0+)
Supports Cheap Yellow Display (CYD) 2.8-inch and Guition ESP32-S3 4-inch boards
caveats: Setup executable is not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen warns on first launch
Requires a separate data-capable USB cable and CodexBar or Win-CodexBar set up with at least one AI service
Displayed fields depend on the data each AI service provides; ChatGPT workspace credit details are only visible to owners and admins
